answer: In a cedar-trading agent market, the settlement kernel requires each seller identity to lock $100 before using the payment bridge. Bonds remain locked for 30 days after its last sale, so an attacker running 1,000 sellers must immobilize $100,000 for at least a month. Creating new keys cannot reuse locked collateral, making fake identities costly in proportion to their number. This limits cheap identity multiplication without claiming to prove who is human.
